## Current CI/CD Shape

Tuturuuu currently automates:

- Vercel preview deployments for non-`production` branches
- Vercel production deployments from the `production` branch
- Independent Vercel preview and production deployments for satellite apps such as `apps/cms`
- Affected-app gating for Vercel deployments before dependency install, build, or deploy work
- Supabase staging migrations driven from `main` and production migrations driven from `production`
- Docker parity and image validation for the self-hosted web runtime
- Modal deployment for `apps/discord`
- Mobile build artifact generation
- Package publishing to npm
- Quality, lint, type, test, and security checks

## Important Repo Conventions

- For most authored changes, run the applicable check, lint, test, and build
  workflows in CI and verify their results on the exact commit. Focused local
  checks help find problems quickly but do not replace that CI evidence. If a
  workflow queue is demonstrably stuck, record the pending jobs and local
  results; resume the exact-commit CI checks before claiming release readiness.
- `ci-check.yml` reads `tuturuuu.ts` and can disable an individual workflow centrally.
- Vercel workflows use `tuturuuu.ts` app metadata and workspace `workspace:*` dependency closures to run only affected app deploys.
- `bun.lock` changes run all Vercel app deploys because lockfile ownership is ambiguous without a source or manifest path.
- Manual `workflow_dispatch` runs enabled workflows even when changed paths would otherwise be unaffected.
- Production Vercel workflows cancel superseded per-app runs only for newer
  `production` pushes. A `main` commit or manual recovery run never cancels an
  active production deployment.
- The external-app internal-package build uses the same cancel-superseded policy, so rapid pushes cannot finish as green no-op builds.
- Database migrations are not treated the same as app deploys; staging and production each have explicit prerequisite logic, with staging now sourced from `main`.
- Docker setup and image-build CI (`docker-setup-check.yaml`) are disabled, including manual dispatch, until explicitly resumed.

## Inline Type Check preflight regressions

`type-check.yaml` runs `node --test --test-reporter=tap
scripts/ci/type-check-inline-workflow.test.js` on its exact checkout with the
`.node-version` Node release,
after the existing Setup Bun step and before dependency installation. Bun is
required by the workflow YAML test helper; these 21 regression cases need no
workspace dependency installation.

The step uses the existing configuration and release-relevance gates. A skipped
step is not test evidence. Before merging a preflight fixture change, verify the
exact-head hosted step succeeded and its TAP summary reports 21 tests, 21 passes,
and zero failures, cancellations, skips, or todos.

## Worker validation caching

Cron Control and Devbox Control run package build, test and type-check tasks
through the existing Turbo remote-cache action with explicit workspace filters.
Meet Realtime uses the same action for build and type-check. Worker builds restore the declared `dist/**` outputs before
emitted-artifact verification. Cron Control and Devbox Control generate binding types before cached type
checks because the generated `.d.ts` file is not a declared type-check output.
Lint, source and emitted runtime checks, SQLite and Durable Object verification,
and deploy dry-runs still run directly. Remote credentials remain step-scoped and
are supplied only to trusted main or production runs, never untrusted PRs.

## Hosted root script qualification

The `Test` workflow runs the complete selection exported by
`scripts/run-script-tests.js` in a separate `Root script tests (24)` job on the
exact checkout. The `(24)` suffix is a stable check name that duplicate-validation
proofs match; the job runs the `.node-version` release (see
[Node.js runtime pin](/build/development-tools/node-runtime)). Node runs it with two test-file workers and the TAP reporter;
the existing paused-runtime discovery policy remains unchanged. No shell glob or
subset replaces the canonical selection.

The job installs the frozen dependencies with the existing Bun setup, verifies
Ruby and `@playwright/test` resolution, and exposes the owning Web dependency
location through `NODE_PATH`. It needs no application secrets, browser install,
workspace build, deployment, or production action. The unit-test aggregation
requires successful package shards or verified duplicate package evidence, and
always requires the fresh root script job to succeed when checks are relevant.

Configuration and release-relevance gates still apply. The root script job does
not reuse the package-shard duplicate-validation result. A skipped job or green
package shards do not prove root script qualification: require the exact-head
job, prerequisite results, complete discovery count, and full TAP summary.
Historical failures remain unresolved until their actual cases pass on the
qualified source; do not infer a fix from a different branch's test bytes.

## Hosted Rust source qualification

On `fix/release-5795-reconciliation` and
`fix/main-production-reconciliation-20261012`, the existing `Test` workflow runs
`Rust source qualification (1.95)` after the shared configuration and release
relevance gates. The read-only job checks out the exact workflow commit, records
its SHA and Cargo manifest/lock hashes, and uses pinned Rust 1.95.0 with two Cargo
build workers. It runs formatting, warning-denying native Clippy, all native
library tests with two test threads, and the wasm Worker target check against the
locked dependency graph. It needs no application secrets or deployment action.

The stable `Unit Tests (24)` aggregate requires this fresh job to succeed on
those branches, including when verified package duplicate evidence skips shards.
A skipped Rust job or successful root script tests do not qualify Rust: require
the exact-head job and its complete Cargo results. Other branches retain their
existing package/root gates. The standalone Rust workflows, TanStack migration,
and backend deployment remain paused; the backend is a future migration target,
and Web continues to serve the live API.

## Cross-app users-core regression tests

The canonical approval regressions live outside the package source tree:

- `packages/users-core/tests/approvals/get-tenant-boundary.test.ts`
- `packages/users-core/tests/approvals/review-reads-tenant-boundary.test.ts`

The source type-check project keeps `rootDir: "src"`. Vitest discovers the
cross-app tests separately through `packages/users-core/vitest.config.ts`;
relocating these tests does not expand the package's source compiler boundary.

That config maps the Web-specific imports `@/lib/post-email-queue` and
`@/features/reports/report-limits` to their exact `apps/web/src` files before
its default `@` alias, which still points to `packages/users-core/src`.
The exact `@tuturuuu/satellite/auth` mapping points to
`packages/satellite/src/auth.ts`; it keeps the satellite namespace separate
from the package-local `@` imports.

Run selected tests from `packages/users-core` with that canonical config and
the receiver's qualified dependencies. For a source `TS6059` error, check that
the cross-app test is outside `src`. For a Vitest module-resolution failure,
check the owning cwd, specific alias destination, and installed dependency
closure before changing compiler roots or alias scope.

A config/source handoff or historical donor test and type results do not prove
the current receiver's test, type, CI, or runtime outcome.

## When To Use This Page

Use this page for orientation. Use the DevOps pages for the runbook you actually need
while operating the system.


### Learn preview build validation

The trusted manual `vercel-preview-learn.yaml` workflow builds the checked-out
`preview_ref` with a 35-minute timeout and the existing two-task Turbo limit.
It records a `build` marker using `git rev-parse HEAD`, rather than the main
workflow dispatch SHA. It does not deploy the artifacts. Learn build markers
cannot advance the successful deployment baseline; existing Platform marker
compatibility remains unchanged. A successful build proves compilation, while
actual-device validation and deployment are separate gates.

Focused checks: `node --test scripts/ci/learn-preview-build.test.js
scripts/ci/github-deployment-markers.test.js scripts/ci/release-workflows.test.js`.

### Generated release inventory

Release Please owns platform and independent package version changes. Release
normalization derives only `apps/docs/reference/repository/versions.mdx` using the
complete documentation inventory generator. Other stale inventory pages fail the
job; this phase does not repair unrelated source or navigation changes.

Before updating the generated PR, the workflow captures its previous immutable
head. A retained versions page must match either the production page, the new
complete projection, or the independently verified projection at that captured
head. Changed generator/configuration sources and unproven docs bytes fail closed.
The amended generated commit keeps its release annotations and is pushed using
its exact head lease. Concurrent updates reject that push. Auto-approval verifies
the final immutable page before rechecking the PR head and base.

`bun git-release-please` also regenerates this page after resolving the platform
version during integration and before validation or commit. Run
`node scripts/ci/release-docs-inventory.js --verify BASE HEAD` to verify immutable
release output. This is derived source evidence, not a publication or deployment
receipt; failed release PR checks continue to block auto-integration.
